author: Ridgway, 1887
status: 겨울철새, 해마다 수백 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
summary: 우리나라에서 흔히 겨울을 나는 겨울철새로, 월동지에서는 작은 무리를 지어 바다 위에서 생활한다. 잠수를 잘해 적이 다가오면 날아오르기보다 물속으로 숨는다. 먹이는 주로 동물성이며 수초도 먹는다. 유라시아와 북아메리카의 아한대에서 한대에 걸쳐 번식하며, 호숫가 풀숲이나 툰드라의 땅 위에 마른풀과 잔가지로 둥지를 짓는다.

art.subject: Stejneger's Scoter (Melanitta stejnegeri), adult male in winter, as seen on Korean coastal seas from November to March: plumage black; a small upturned white crescent below and behind the eye; secondaries white, showing as a white patch at the rear of the folded wing. Bill long and deep with a hooked nail, mostly orange-yellow becoming orange-red towards the tip, with a prominent black knob rising at the base of the upper mandible; iris whitish; legs and feet reddish-pink.
art.pose: swimming on the sea, about to dive
art.scene: Korean winter coast: open grey sea with a gentle swell offshore; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view swimming: black plumage, small white crescent under and behind the pale eye, white secondaries just visible on the folded wing, orange-yellow bill with a black knob at the base
adult female, side view swimming: dark brown overall, two pale patches on the face (in front of the eye and on the ear coverts), dark bill without a knob, white secondaries just visible
adult male, flight side view from above: all-black body and wings with a large white panel on the secondaries
art.build: Large, heavy sea duck, 56cm, about Mallard length but bulkier and lower in the water. Large head with a long sloping forehead running into the knobbed bill; bill about as long as the head, deep at the base. Floats low and dives readily in small groups offshore, diving rather than flying when approached. Legs short, set far back. At rest the white secondaries may show as a small white patch on the folded wing. Tail short and pointed. Flight heavy and direct, with a large white rectangular patch on the secondaries contrasting with the black wing.
avoid: Do not paint the knob yellow; on this species the knob is black and the colour is on the rest of the bill (a yellow knob is Black Scoter).
Do not omit the white secondaries or the small white eye crescent.
Do not paint a dark iris on the male; it is pale.
Do not draw a small stubby bill; the bill is long, deep and knobbed.
